gaps.quoted_evidence: Co-Founder & CEO, Co-Founder & COO, Head of Development, Head of Operations
gaps.reasoning: The full named team consists of two founders (CEO, COO) plus a Head of Development and a Head of Operations. No title anywhere in the leadership reflects sales, commercial, growth or revenue ownership, and the company is already operating a paid engagement with a named retail customer (Holland & Barrett) with no visible commercial owner driving expansion or new logo acquisition.
gaps.what_goes_wrong: Founder-led selling caps growth rate and creates a bottleneck: pipeline, pricing negotiation and account expansion depend entirely on CEO/COO bandwidth, and there is no repeatable process for winning the next retailer beyond the first reference customer.
gaps.name: Commercial and revenue leader
gaps.covers: First repeatable revenue engine. Moving off founder led selling.
gaps.profile: Has built a first revenue function from nothing, not inherited one. Carried a number. Has hired and managed the first two or three sellers.

open_questions: No funding amount, investor names or round stage is stated anywhere in the evidence, so it is unclear whether a fractional CFO or fundraising support gap applies at all - this is an absence, not a positive signal.

Physical operations (e-cargo bike fleet, store-level inventory) are visible, but a 'Head of Operations' title is already present; it is unclear from the evidence whether this role has senior supply-chain depth or is more junior/generalist, so an operations-supply-chain gap cannot be confidently asserted.
No pricing is visible, but it is unclear whether this is a deliberate enterprise-style 'contact us' model (normal for this category) or an unaddressed pricing gap.

demotions.contradicting_evidence: Holland & Barrett - approximately 100 stores in London supported with e-cargo bikes and inventory analytics software. A named enterprise customer (100-store national retailer) directly contradicts the claim that the company lacks enterprise sales capability. The company has already successfully sold into and is operating a complex multi-site retail account, which is evidence of enterprise sales execution, not evidence of a gap.

notes_for_human: Evidence is thin - only four named team members and one customer logo across three pages. The two gaps flagged (commercial leadership, enterprise sales) rest on the same underlying fact pattern: a founder-heavy team with operational/technical titles, one large multi-site retail account, and no visible commercial hire. Confidence is capped at medium because each rests on a single clear source rather than two independent corroborating signals. Roles that already appear filled (Head of Development for technical leadership, Head of Operations for supply chain/ops) were deliberately excluded per the disqualifier rule, even though the physical-product and logistics signals would otherwise map to those archetypes.
